title: Choose the visual world for Cafe POS
question: The roll assigned Hotelware. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Hotelware
options.lineage: Heavy vitrified restaurant china with a banded rim and a maker's backstamp
options.thesis: The till dressed like the café's own crockery: china-white ground, one bottle-green rim band marking whatever is live.
options.viewport: Bottle-green nav rail; menu grid of flat white tiles each with its category's thin rim band; order panel whose amount due sits inside a double green band, with the total set wide like a backstamp.
options.risk: If the band is used everywhere it turns into decoration; it must only mark live state.

raised.raise: State is carried by band form, not only hue: solid double = live, single = idle, dashed = waiting to sync or not yet sent, struck = void.
Every menu tile is one fixed size on one grid, with prices on a shared baseline, so the eye scans a column of prices without hunting.
All money is tabular and right-aligned tight to the panel edge; the totals block is pinned and never scrolls away.
A table code is one identity everywhere: the same chip in the order header, the orders list and the floor plan.

options.label: Guest Check Pad
options.thesis: Every order is the next numbered check torn off the pad.
options.viewport: Green-tinted shell, menu grid on white, order panel styled as the current numbered check with a red serial.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most café POS redesigns land, and its ruled lines can slide into costume.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: Order numbers and tables signed like gates: one message per band, numbers at monumental scale.
options.viewport: Black shell, yellow band header naming the current order and table monumentally, menu grid in black and white.
options.case: Clarity is excellent, especially for the kitchen and pickup, but café staff do not see their world in it.
options.risk: A full yellow shell is loud for an eight-hour shift.

options.label: Plate Section
options.lineage: Design annual plate pages: hairlines, registration marks, one grotesque
options.thesis: A precise, quiet grid of hairlines where one periwinkle seal marks the action.
options.viewport: Hairline-ruled menu grid, a sticky token bar of order facts, black square primary buttons.
options.case: Holds product clarity with superb discipline; loses on audience: it reads as a studio tool, not a café.
options.risk: Cold and low-contrast on touch targets.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one rail; colour only as hairline emission lines.
options.viewport: A charcoal plate with one off-centre rail.
options.case: Loses on both axes: staff mid-rush cannot read state from line height.
options.kept: State carried by line form (solid, dashed, doubled), not hue alone.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Fixed-scale plates on one shared baseline.
options.case: Loses on both axes; cream and serif is also the AI default for cafés.
options.kept: One fixed tile size and a shared price baseline.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Tracklists timed tight to the margin.
options.case: Loses on both axes: handwriting harms legibility of prices.
options.kept: Right-aligned tabular figures tight to the edge; the totals never overflow.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.lineage: Newsprint circle catalogs keyed to a hall map
options.thesis: A grid cell and its place on the map are the same thing.
options.case: Loses on both axes: too dense and too grey for a counter.
options.kept: Table codes as one identity across the list and the floor plan.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern counter POS like the market leaders, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, category tabs, white item cards, cart on the right with a blue charge button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other till by design.
